Update.Headline: Extended by New York
Update.Notes: Newsome (concussion) agreed Tuesday with the Giants on a three-year $46 million extension that includes $32 million guaranteed, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
Update.Analysis: Newsome joined the Giants in the offseason on a one-year, $8 million deal, but he earned himself some longer-term security with his standout play to begin the campaign. Before a concussion kept him out for the Giants' Week 7 win over Houston, the 26-year-old cornerback recorded 25 tackles (17 solo), six pass breakups and one interception through the team's first six games.

Update.Headline: Signed to active roster
Update.Notes: The Cardinals signed Wallace from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Wallace signed to Arizona's practice squad in August and has yet to play in a regular-season game. Week 9 will be the undrafted free agent's NFL debut should he be active for Sunday's matchup against Seattle. He will likely act as a depth piece should he play.

Update.Headline: Unavailable next four weeks
Update.Notes: The Cardinals placed Yeboah (undisclosed) on the practice squad injured list Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Yeboah reverted to Arizona's practice squad Monday after logging no offensive snaps and just 20 snaps on special teams. The 28-year-old is unavailable for at least the next four games after being placed on the practice squad IR. Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins still lead the way at tight end.

Update.Headline: Re-signs to practice squad
Update.Notes: The Cardinals re-signed Fairweather to the practice squad, Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Fairweather spent time with Arizona in the offseason, leading the NFL with 13 catches during the preseason. The 24-year-old will likely take on a depth role at tight end with Kenny Yeboah unavailable for the next four weeks after landing on practice squad IR.

Update.Headline: Scooped up by Saints
Update.Notes: The Saints claimed Estime off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: New Orleans released kicker Daniel Carlson to clear room on the 53-man roster for Estime, who began the season with the Saints before being cut on an injury settlement Sept. 22. After moving past a thigh injury, Estime caught on with the Browns and made his lone appearance for the team back in Week 6, when he carried nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Ravens. Upon rejoining the Saints, Estime will provide depth to a backfield that also includes Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson (shoulder).

Update.Headline: Lands extension after strong start to 2026
Update.Notes: Adebawore agreed Tuesday with the Colts on a two-year, $35 million contract extension, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
Update.Analysis: Per Pelissero, the deal includes a $13 million signing bonus and $22.5 million in new money through next season. A 2023 fourth-round draft pick, Adebawore had been in the final year of his rookie deal and was considered a potential trade chip leading up to the Nov. 10 deadline, but the Colts have instead elected to keep him around on a longer-term basis. Through the Colts' first eight games of the season, 25-year-old defensive tackle has matched the career-best total of four sacks he posted over a 17-game slate in 2025. Adebawore has also added 19 tackles and two pass breakups.

Update.Headline: Appealing trade target for number of teams
Update.Notes: Thomas has drawn interest from other teams leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Ian Rapoport of ESPN reports.
Update.Analysis: Since delivering an 87-1,282-10 receiving line over 17 games as a rookie in 2024, Thomas' production has cratered in the ensuing two seasons. He's been firmly behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) in terms of snap share through the Jaguars' first seven games and has drawn more than three targets in just one of those contests. Though the vertical threat Thomas presents might make him an appealing target for teams seeking a big-play receiver, it's unclear if the Jaguars have much motivation to move him. Despite his declining role within the Jacksonville offense, Thomas remains under contract through next season at relatively modest cap hits of $4.01 million in 2026 and $4.66 million in 2027.

Update.Headline: Set to kick for Saints in Week 9
Update.Notes: The Saints plan to elevate or sign Smyth off their practice squad to handle kicking duties in Sunday's game against the Browns, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
Update.Analysis: Daniel Carlson handled kicking duties for the Saints through their first seven games, but after he misfired on four field-goal tries and two extra-point attempts, he was released Monday. The Saints will now give Smyth another look, after he had served as their kicker in the final six games of last season before being cut loose following the preseason. Smyth fared well in his first taste of NFL action in 2025, going 12-for-16 on field goals and 13-for-13 on extra points, with two of his misses coming from beyond 50 yards.

Update.Headline: Churns out full practice
Update.Notes: Hill (groin) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice.
Update.Analysis: After the Ravens estimated him as a limited practice participant Monday on their initial Week 9 injury report, Hill took every rep Tuesday to clear up any concern about his availability heading into Thursday's game against the Jaguars. Hill should serve in his familiar role as the Ravens' top passing-down back in Week 9, with Derrick Henry continuing to lead the way on the ground.

Update.Headline: Returning to Washington
Update.Notes: The Commanders claimed Henry off waivers from the Seahawks on Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: After being cut by Seattle on Monday, Henry quickly caught on with the Commanders. The 2026 undrafted free agent out of UTSA had previously joined the Commanders for training camp and the preseason, only to be waived prior to Week 1. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve for at least two more games and Jeremy McNichols (foot) likely to miss the remainder of the season, Henry will provide the Commanders with another option in the backfield behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler. Henry didn't end up making his NFL debut during his time on the Seahawks roster.

Update.Headline: Cut by Minnesota
Update.Notes: Nesbit was cut from the Vikings' practice squad Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Nesbit was signed to the practice squad with Minnesota on Oct. 28, but he will now potentially look for another opportunity elsewhere. The tight end has yet to make his NFL regular-season debut, and his next destination will likely be with a team's practice unit.

Update.Headline: Placed on IR
Update.Notes: Kinlaw (knee) was placed on injured reserve by the Commanders on Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Kinlaw suffered a knee injury in Week 6 versus San Francisco, and he was ultimately forced to miss the team's Week 8 win over the Eagles. The defensive lineman will now be sidelined for at least four more contests before he'd be eligible to return to action Dec. 6 versus the Titans.

Update.Headline: Officially placed on IR
Update.Notes: Payne (foot) was placed on injured reserve by the Commanders on Tuesday, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
Update.Analysis: Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in his left foot during practice last week. His transition to injured reserve comes as no surprise, and in Payne's absence, Tim Settle will operate as the team's primary nose tackle moving forward.

Update.Headline: Set for lead-back duties
Update.Notes: Allgeier is slated to work as Arizona's No. 1 running back beginning with Sunday's game at Seattle after Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
Update.Analysis: After previously leading the Cardinals backfield when Love was sidelined due to a different ankle injury Weeks 6 and 7, Allgeier is now slated for a longer run atop the depth chart while Love is projected to miss 4-to-5 weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain. Love sustained his latest ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys, with his early exit clearing the way for Allgeier to run wild. Allgeier finished with a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five receptions. In addition to Love getting hurt, Bam Knight sustained a concussion and is uncertain to play Week 9 against Seattle, so the backfield could belong to Allgeier, Evan Hull and a practice-squad signee (likely Jerome Ford). Though Allgeier found substantial success in Week 8, he came into the contest averaging just 2.9 yards per carry on 61 totes. He'll also be facing a Seattle defense that is tied for the second-fewest yards per carry (3.8) allowed to running backs this season, so a repeat performance by Allgeier would be surprising.

Update.Headline: Signed by Denver
Update.Notes: Patterson was signed to the Broncos' practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official website reports.
Update.Analysis: Patterson was cut from the Browns' practice squad Oct. 27, but he has now found another opportunity with Denver. With RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve for at least three more games, Patterson will provide the Broncos with another option in the backfield behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.

Update.Headline: Cut by Denver
Update.Notes: Pancol was cut from the Broncos' practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official website reports.
Update.Analysis: Pancol will return to the open market after inking a deal to join Denver's practice squad Oct. 27. The wide receiver's next opportunity will likely come as a member of another practice squad.

Update.Headline: Let go by Denver
Update.Notes: Ross was cut from the Broncos' practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official website reports.
Update.Analysis: Ross joined Denver's practice squad Oct. 6, but he failed to be elevated to the active roster for any contests prior to being let go Tuesday. The wide receiver signed with the team in May as an undrafted free agent, and he may return to the Broncos' practice squad in the near future.

Update.Headline: Not expected to return Week 9
Update.Notes: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Tuesday that Conner (foot) won't return from IR this week, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
Update.Analysis: Though LaFleur said last week that Conner could "potentially" play this season, that won't happen in Week 9. The veteran running back continues to work his way back from a right foot injury and has not yet been cleared to practice. Arizona is dealing with multiple injuries in its backfield, including Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion), so Conner could provide a big boost once he's able to work his way back this week. Instead, the team will turn to Tyler Allgeier to lead its backfield, with Evan Hull serving as his primary backup if Knight is unable to suit up Sunday against Seattle.

Update.Headline: Climbs up depth chart
Update.Notes: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However,the Cardinals have since traded away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, so Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026 on Sunday, coincidentally against his former teams the Cowboys. He wasn't much of a factor in a comeback win, however, earning just one target for a 17-yard reception while taking the field for 40 of the team's 81 offensive play. While Fehoko could see his playing time climb even higher in Week 9, tight ends Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, wideout Michael Wilson (ribs) and running back Tyler Allgeier may be better bets to command targets from quarterback Gardner Minshew.

Update.Headline: Placed on IR
Update.Notes: Ebukam (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve by the Falcons on Tuesday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official website reports.
Update.Analysis: Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9 versus the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result of the injury. In his absence, Za'Darius Smith is a top candidate to operate in a more prominent role at outside linebacker.

Update.Headline: Signs to Cleveland's practice squad
Update.Notes: Guillory agreed to a contract to join the Browns' practice squad Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Guillory had previously spent time in Baltimore's organization before being cut from the Ravens' practice squad in mid-October. He'll now have a chance to make an impression with the Browns in the hope of eventually being summoned for his first regular-season NFL action. Cleveland currently has a healthy wideout corps, so Guillory isn't likely to be elevated for Sunday's matchup against the Saints.

Update.Headline: Cut from practice squad injured list
Update.Notes: The Browns cut Means (knee) from their practice squad injured list Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Means signed to Cleveland's practice squad in early September but landed on the practice-squad injured list due to a knee injury Oct. 20. The 2024 fifth-round draft selection has now been cut, so he'll have a chance to look for work with another organization once he gets healthy. The Browns signed wideout Xavier Guillory to their practice squad in a corresponding move Tuesday.

Update.Headline: Let go by New England
Update.Notes: Dorner was cut from the Patriots' practice squad Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Dorner joined the team's practice squad in early September after signing with New England as an undrafted free agent in May. The wide receiver failed to appear in any regular-season contests before being let go Tuesday, and he may now have to look for another opportunity elsewhere.

Update.Headline: Loses spot on Philadelphia's practice squad
Update.Notes: The Eagles cut Skinner from their practice squad Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Skinner just joined the Eagles' practice squad last week, so his time in the organization was short. The Kansas product has one game of regular-season NFL experience on his resume, during which he caught one pass for 10 yards on one target in Week 18 of last season while with the Jets. Skinner is now free to seek work with another club.

Update.Headline: Officially goes to IR
Update.Notes: The Jaguars placed Hamilton (knee) on their injured reserve list Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Hamilton suffered a ruptured quad during Sunday's game versus the Colts, and now he'll spend the rest of the season on IR. His departure from Jacksonville's defensive line figures to open up more opportunities for 2024 second-rounder Ruke Orhorhoro as the campaign continues.

Update.Headline: Works out with Arizona
Update.Notes: Bradley (thumb) was hosted for a workout with the Cardinals on Tuesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
Update.Analysis: Bradley was waived by the Jaguars after reaching an injury settlement with the team in September after suffering a thumb injury. The quarterback now appears to be back to full health, and he'll look to latch on with a new squad.

Update.Headline: Back to full health
Update.Notes: Jefferson (undisclosed) was hosted for a workout with the Cardinals on Tuesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
Update.Analysis: Jefferson was waived after reaching an injury settlement with the Vikings in September after suffering an undisclosed injury during the preseason. The running back now appears to be fully healthy, and he'll have a chance to sign with a new squad at the halfway point of the regular season.

Update.Headline: Officially placed on IR
Update.Notes: The Jaguars placed Murray (elbow) on their injured reserve list Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: It was already known Murray suffered a season-ending elbow injury during the first quarter of Sunday's game versus the Colts, so the move comes as no big surprise. In his absence, 2025 sixth-rounder Rayuan Lane could step into a starting role at safety for the rest of the year.

Update.Headline: Parts ways with Rams
Update.Notes: The Rams released Bachman on Tuesday, Blaine Grisak of SI.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Bachman was signed to Los Angeles' active roster Oct. 3, but he logged just three offensive snaps and didn't draw any targets during his five games with the club. He did, however, have a significant role as both a kickoff and punt returner. Jordan Whittington could be asked to take on those responsibilities now that Bachman is no longer on the team.

Update.Headline: Tries out with Dolphins
Update.Notes: Miami worked out Rucker (undisclosed) on Tuesday, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
Update.Analysis: Two weeks after the Raiders waived him from their injured reserve list, Rucker appears to be back in football shape and is looking for a new team. The Dolphins have arguably the weakest group of wide receivers in the league, so any additions they make at the position in 2026 will be worth keeping an eye on.

Update.Headline: Works out with Seattle
Update.Notes: Curtis (knee) was hosted for a workout with the Seahawks on Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
Update.Analysis: Curtis appears to be back to full health after reaching an injury settlement with the Jets in September after suffering a knee injury during the preseason. The tight end has yet to make his NFL regular-season debut after going undrafted in April, and his next destination will likely be as a member of a team's practice squad.

Update.Headline: Moves to injured reserve
Update.Notes: Connors (hand) was placed on IR on Tuesday, Blaine Grisak of SI.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Connors broke his hand in Sunday's win over the Chargers and is slated for surgery. He's worked as a core special-teamer this season but hasn't logged a snap on offense. As such, Connors' IR stint -- which will last at least four games -- isn't likely to cause any waves in fantasy.

Update.Headline: Looking good for Thursday
Update.Notes: Smith (foot) was a full participant at practice Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Smith popped up on Baltimore's injury report Monday with a foot issue, but it doesn't look like it was anything too serious, and he's on track to play in Week 9. He's easily on pace for his fourth consecutive 100-plus tackle season and is a solid IDP consideration in most formats going into Thursday's game versus the Jaguars.

Update.Headline: Back with practice squad
Update.Notes: Foster reverted to the Seahawks' practice squad Tuesday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
Update.Analysis: Foster was elevated to the active roster ahead of Monday night's 34-17 loss to the Bears. The wide receiver played three snaps on special teams in the contest, and he can be elevated two more times before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

Update.Headline: Still dealing with rib issue
Update.Notes: Walker (ribs) was a limited participant at practice Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Walker suffered a rib injury during the third quarter of Sunday's game versus the Colts, and now his status for Thursday's game at Baltimore is uncertain. He'll probably need to upgrade to full participation at practice Wednesday to avoid carrying an injury designation into gameday.

Update.Headline: Goes back to practice squad
Update.Notes: Carlson reverted to the Bears' practice squad Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction log.
Update.Analysis: Carlson was elevated ahead of Chicago's win over Seattle on Monday and logged 10 offensive snaps, along with four special-teams snaps, without otherwise getting into the box score. It was his first game-day action of the season, so the veteran tight end is eligible to be elevated twice more. With Cole Kmet (knee) landing on season-ending IR in late October, Carlson could be called upon again in Week 9 against Tampa Bay.

Update.Headline: Tending to shoulder soreness
Update.Notes: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Tuesday that Darrisaw is nursing a shoulder issue, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Darrisaw played all 52 of the Vikings' offensive snaps during Sunday's game at Detroit, but he hurt his shoulder somewhere along the way, and now his status for Week 9 is in doubt. His activity at practice will be worth monitoring when Minnesota releases its first official injury report of the week Thursday.

Update.Headline: Placed on IR
Update.Notes: Howell (wrist) was placed on injured reserve by the Bengals on Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

Update.Headline: Activated from IR
Update.Notes: Bryant (ankle) was activated from injured reserve by the Patriots on Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Bryant will return to action in Week 9 after spending the entirety of the regular season to this point on IR after suffering an ankle injury during the preseason. The 24-year-old will operate as a top reserve option behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses at offensive tackle moving forward.

Update.Headline: Let go by New England
Update.Notes: Vildor was released by the Patriots on Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Vildor will hit the open market after compiling seven total tackles (six solo), a pass defensed and a forced fumble while appearing in the Patriots' last five contests. The cornerback could return to the practice squad with New England in the near future.

Update.Headline: Has practice window opened
Update.Notes: Christensen (hamstring) was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all season and has yet to play in a game. The Panthers will now have 21 days to activate him from IR, otherwise he won't be eligible to suit up this season. If Christensen does indeed return, he could be moved into a starting role.

Update.Headline: Gets clearance to practice again
Update.Notes: The Falcons designated Abdullah (hamstring) for return to practice from their injured reserve list Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction log.
Update.Analysis: Abdullah went to Atlanta's injured reserve list after hurting his hamstring back in Week 4 at New Orleans, but it now looks like he may be close to returning to game action. The transaction opens a 21-day window during which the Falcons can officially activate Abdullah from IR before they'd have to put him back on the shelf for the rest of the campaign.

Update.Headline: Works out with San Francisco
Update.Notes: Long (undisclosed) was hosted for a tryout with the 49ers on Tuesday, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Long was released from injured reserve by the Saints on Thursday after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on injured reserve with an undisclosed injury. The cornerback now appears to be back to full health, and he'll have a chance to latch on with a new squad in the near future.

Update.Headline: Cut by Philadelphia
Update.Notes: The Eagles removed Bennett (knee) from injured reserve Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Bennett had been on IR due to a knee injury all season but was designated to return Oct. 14. He appeared to be back to health, as he was a full participant in each of Philadelphia's past seven practices, but with his 21-day practice window close to expiring, the Eagles decided to part ways with him rather than activate him. Bennett has started in 12 of his 35 NFL regular-season appearances, and he could be an appealing target for clubs in need of depth in the secondary.

Update.Headline: Goes to IR
Update.Notes: The Jets placed Mitchell (concussion) on their injured reserve list Tuesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
Update.Analysis: In a corresponding transaction, the Jets signed tackle Blake Freeland to their active roster. Mitchell, who has not made a start on the offensive line yet this season, will now have to miss at least the next four games.

Update.Headline: Gets removed from IR
Update.Notes: The Jets removed Brown (finger) from their injured reserve list Tuesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
Update.Analysis: Brown has been on the Jets' injured reserve list since before their regular-season opener, and he's now becoming a free agent again. Over 10 games with the Rams and the Jets in 2025, he recorded eight tackles (four solo).

Update.Headline: Healthy ahead of Week 9
Update.Notes: Ioane (knee) was a full participant at the Ravens' practice Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: Ioane is set to return to action Thursday night against the Jaguars after missing Week 8 with a sprained MCL in his right knee that he suffered in Week 7 against the Bengals. The 22-year-old will likely be back in his starting role at right guard versus Jacksonville.

Update.Headline: Officially put on IR
Update.Notes: Rolder (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
Update.Analysis: This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

Update.Headline: Makes four grabs Sunday
Update.Notes: Spann-Ford caught four of five targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.
Update.Analysis: Starting tight end Jake Ferguson logged only four offensive snaps before leaving Sunday's contest with an ankle injury, and Spann-Ford ended up playing a career-high 65 offensive snaps as a result. He ended up second on the team in targets behind CeeDee Lamb (11), and he could be worth a look as a streaming option in deeper formats if Ferguson is unable to suit up in Week 9 at Indianapolis.

Update.Headline: Seven carries in Week 8
Update.Notes: Kiner rushed seven times for 38 yards during Sunday's 24-19 win over Miami.
Update.Analysis: Kiner operated as the top reserve option behind starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson in Week 8, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined. Kiner has compiled 160 rushing yards on 28 carries while reeling in his only target for seven yards over the team's last four contests, and he could earn more opportunities moving forward.

Update.Headline: Five catches in victory
Update.Notes: Chism caught all five of his targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
Update.Analysis: Chism led the team in targets and receptions, with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) unavailable. The wide receiver played a season-high 88 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and he has now reeled in 15 of 20 targets for 151 yards and a touchdown over seven regular-season contests with New England so far this year.

Update.Headline: Held in check Sunday
Update.Notes: Goodson took seven carries for 14 yards and caught both of his two targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.
Update.Analysis: Dallas wasn't really able to get anything going on the ground in Week 8, totaling just 93 rushing yards on 39 carries. Just like the offense as a whole, Goodson found a bit more success in the passing game, and he posted his best receiving total since back in 2024. As long as starter Javonte Williams remains available, though, Goodson should stay in a change-of-pace role.

Update.Headline: Inefficient with six targets Sunday
Update.Notes: Cooper caught two of six targets for 19 yards Sunday in a Week 8 loss to Washington.
Update.Analysis: Both of Cooper's catches came in the first half -- he didn't haul in any of his three targets in the second half. The second-year wideout led Eagles wideouts with 66 offensive snaps and finished second with the six targets, but it didn't amount to much production, as he couldn't form much of a connection with QB Tanner McKee. Despite an elevated role due to injuries to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) the past two weeks, Cooper has just three catches for 36 yards in that span, making him an unappealing fantasy option.

Update.Headline: Two catches in overtime win
Update.Notes: Duvernay caught both of his targets for 14 yards while also adding 75 yards as a kick returner and 12 punt-return yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Cowboys.
Update.Analysis: Duvernay reeled in his first two passes of the year while playing 34 offensive snaps in the victory. Fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) fractured his right tibia during the contest, and he is likely set to miss the rest of the 2026 campaign. Duvernay will likely see an increased role on offense in Bourne's absence, but he will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup against Seattle.

Update.Headline: Increased opportunities ahead
Update.Notes: Virgil failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory against Dallas.
Update.Analysis: Virgil played a season-high 38 offensive snaps, but he went without a reception for the third straight week. The Cardinals placed Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) on injured reserve Tuesday after the wide receiver fractured his right tibia in Week 8, so more opportunities could come Virgil's way moving forward. Regardless of an increase in workload, the team's Week 9 matchup versus Seattle will be a challenging one for the 22-year-old.

Update.Headline: Logs two catches in Week 8 loss
Update.Notes: Brown finished Sunday's loss to the Commanders with two catches for 17 yards on two targets.
Update.Analysis: With both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) missing the contest, Brown ranked third among Eagles wideouts with 32 offensive snaps. He didn't do much with the opportunity, as the veteran wideout notched just two receptions for the second straight week. If Smith and/or Wicks return in Week 9 against the Giants, Brown may see his role diminish.

Update.Headline: Gets involved in blowout win
Update.Notes: Johnson took four carries for four yards and caught all three of his targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 36-10 win versus the Ravens.
Update.Analysis: In a game that Buffalo ran away with in the second half, Johnson's four carries were a season high, but he couldn't produce much on those rush attempts. Ray Davis actually saw more carries (six) in Week 8 and was more effective as a rusher (30 yards). As long as lead back James Cook is available, Johnson won't have much utility in most fantasy formats.

Update.Headline: Catchless in Week 8
Update.Notes: Moore did not garner a target during Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
Update.Analysis: Moore was held without a catch for the first time since Week 5, failing to take advantage of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) being unavailable. Moore figures to remain an afterthought on offense in Week 9 against the Giants.

Update.Headline: Draws two targets in loss
Update.Notes: Cuevas caught one of two targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 36-10 loss at Buffalo.
Update.Analysis: Cuevas played 13 offensive snaps in Week 8, again trailing behind veteran Mark Andrews (29) and rookie fourth-rounder Matthew Hibner (21). With that said, Cuevas ran routes on most of those snaps, and he drew multiple targets for the fourth straight game Sunday. He still won't be a viable fantasy option in most formats as long as Andrews and Hibner remain healthy.

Update.Headline: Draws season-high four targets in Week 8
Update.Notes: Higgins tallied two catches for 10 yards on four targets Sunday in a 33-30 overtime win over Dallas.
Update.Analysis: Wideout Michael Wilson missed a portion of the contest due to an injury to his ribs, and Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) exited for good late in the first half. That resulted in a need for other Cardinals pass catchers to step up, and Higgins ended up getting targeted a season-high four times. However, he didn't do much with the opportunity, finishing with his lowest yardage total since he was shut out in Week 2. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Trey McBride had another big game with seven catches for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. McBride's elite status will likely continue to make Higgins an afterthought most weeks.

Update.Headline: One catch in Week 8
Update.Notes: Treadwell caught one of two targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars.
Update.Analysis: Treadwell failed to record multiple receptions in a game for the first time since Week 3 against Houston. The wide receiver could be set to operate in a more prominent role if the team decides to deal fellow wideout Josh Downs prior to the trade deadline Nov. 10. For the time being, Treadwell doesn't figure to have much fantasy appeal Sunday against the Cowboys.

Update.Headline: Another quiet performance Week 8
Update.Notes: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory.
Update.Analysis: Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

Update.Headline: No catches in Week 8
Update.Notes: Johnson did not garner a target during Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.
Update.Analysis: Johnson and the rest of the Buccaneers' pass catchers went without receptions in Week 8 as quarterback Baker Mayfield failed to complete a pass on three attempts in the team's rain-soaked victory. The wide receiver may have another chance to operate in a prominent role on offense if fellow wideout Emeka Egbuka (foot) remains unavailable Sunday versus the Bears.

Update.Headline: Two offensive snaps versus Rams
Update.Notes: Lambert-Smith did not garner a target during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
Update.Analysis: Lambert-Smith was expected to revert back to a minimal role on offense in Week 8 due to both Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris returning to action, and that is exactly what happened. Lambert-Smith played just two offensive snaps in the contest, and he will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as the rest of the Chargers' primary pass catchers are healthy.

Update.Headline: Gets no targets in return
Update.Notes: Bech finished without a target or touch in Sunday's 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.
Update.Analysis: Bech returned from a four-game absence due to a forearm injury and logged a 40 percent offensive snap share, but he didn't get any looks from QB Kirk Cousins. In fact, Cousins didn't go to his wideout corps as a whole very often -- 16 of his 26 targets went to tight ends, and another four went to running back Ashton Jeanty. Bech will look to get back into the box score Sunday in a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

Update.Headline: Secures pick-six in victory
Update.Notes: Lane recorded four total tackles (one solo) and three passes defensed, including a pick-six, during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
Update.Analysis: Lane played every one of the team's defensive snaps in Week 8, stepping into a starting role in the secondary with Antonio Johnson (ankle) unavailable. The 23-year-old's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter when he jumped in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones for an interception, returning it 92 yards for his first career defensive touchdown. Lane has now compiled 20 total tackles (10 solo) and four passes defensed, including Sunday's pick-six, over seven contests during the 2026 campaign.

Update.Headline: Doesn't haul in only target Week 8
Update.Notes: Cameron did not catch his lone target in a 42-7 rout of the Colts on Sunday. He returned one punt for six yards and one kickoff for 18 yards.
Update.Analysis: Jacksonville didn't need to go to its air-game much given the easy win, and QB Trevor Lawrence threw just 14 passes. None of those went to Cameron -- his only target (which he didn't catch) came from backup signal-caller Quinn Ewers in garbage time. Cameron did log a season-high 52 percent offensive snap share, but game script didn't do him any favors in terms of production. With no catches in three of his seven games this season, Cameron doesn't make for an appealing fantasy asset.

Update.Headline: Notches sack in blowout win
Update.Notes: Oluokun recorded nine total tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 42-7 win against the Colts.
Update.Analysis: Oluokun led the team in takedowns, notching at least eight tackles for the third straight game. The linebacker was also able to get to quarterback Daniel Jones for his first sack of the year in the second quarter, matching his season total from both the 2024 and 2025 campaigns. Oluokun is as steady as it gets from a fantasy perspective, and he has now registered 51 total tackles (31 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two interceptions and a forced fumble over seven contests to open the regular season.

Update.Headline: Secures interception in loss
Update.Notes: Wheatley recorded seven total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Thursday night's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
Update.Analysis: Wheatley was able to secure a career-high seven stops, while his biggest play of the game came in the fourth quarter when he picked off a deep pass from Packers quarterback Jordan Love. The interception was the first of the Wheatley's career, and the rookie has now compiled 26 total tackles (19 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over six contests during the 2026 campaign.

Update.Headline: Ties season high with 10 stops Week 8
Update.Notes: Starks finished Sunday's loss to Buffalo with 10 tackles (five solo).
Update.Analysis: Starks was quite active as a tackler, finishing second on the Ravens in stops behind Roquan Smith (11). It was the second time Starks has notched double-digit tackles in a game this season, though he's averaged a more modest 5.2 stops in his other six games. With 51 total tackles through eight contests, he's on pace to exceed the 84 stops he recorded across 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year.

Update.Headline: Double-digit stops in win
Update.Notes: Williams recorded 10 total tackles (seven solo) during Thursday night's 27-19 win over the Panthers.
Update.Analysis: Williams finished tied for the team lead in takedowns with linebacker Isaiah McDuffie, notching double-digit stops for the fourth time this season. The safety has now compiled 71 total tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding six passes defensed, two of which are interceptions, and a fumble recovery over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

Update.Headline: Comes up huge in Week 8 win
Update.Notes: Hopper recorded eight tackles, including 1.0 sacks, and three defensed passes, including an interception, in last Thursday's 27-19 victory over Carolina.
Update.Analysis: Hopper finished third on Green Bay with his eight stops but that was only one part of his impactful performance. The third-year linebacker picked off Bryce Young in the backfield in the second quarter to give the Packers the ball in Carolina territory, and he sacked Young early in the third period on a drive that ended in a Panthers punt. Hopper has started and logged more than a 90 percent defensive snap share each of the past two weeks, and given his performance against Carolina, he doesn't figure to give up that role soon.

Update.Headline: Racks up 10 stops in Week 8 victory
Update.Notes: McDuffie finished last Thursday's 27-19 win over Carolina with 10 tackles (three solo).
Update.Analysis: McDuffie tied with Evan Williams for the team lead in tackles. He played every one of the Packers' defensive snaps for the second straight game in the absence of Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie has tallied 21 tackles in the pair of contests, so he's looking like a strong IDP option, at least for as long as Franklin remains sidelined.

Update.Headline: Tallies 13 tackles on Monday Night Football
Update.Notes: Jones recorded 13 tackles and a defensed pass in Monday's Week 8 loss to Chicago.
Update.Analysis: Jones not only led Seattle in stops in the loss, he also tied the season-high mark he first established in Week 1 versus New England. The veteran linebacker continues to be an impactful IDP asset in his sixth NFL campaign, as he ranks third in the NFL with 81 tackles through eight weeks. Jones has recorded at least eight stops in every one of his appearances this season.

Update.Headline: Posts another huge tackle tally Week 8
Update.Notes: Singleton notched 14 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and defensed a pass in Sunday's 28-24 victory against the Chiefs.
Update.Analysis: Singleton continued to rack up a vast number of stops -- it was the fifth time this season he's recorded double-digit tackles. The star linebacker also registered a sack for the second straight week, coming up huge when he brought down Patrick Mahomes for a six-yard loss late in the fourth quarter on third down. The next play was a missed Harrison Butker 54-yard field-goal try, which led to Denver pulling off the comeback with a touchdown less than a minute later. Singleton has been an elite IDP asset in fantasy this season, as he leads the NFL by a wide margin with 101 tackles through eight weeks.

Update.Headline: Posts 10 stops in Week 8 loss
Update.Notes: Cashman finished Sunday's loss to Detroit with 10 tackles (five solo).
Update.Analysis: Cashman was one of four Vikings to notch double-digit stops in the team's first loss of the season. The veteran linebacker has recorded at least seven stops in each of his seven games this season and has registered double-digit tackles three times. He's well beyond pace for a fourth consecutive season of triple-digit tackles, as he already has 64 stops (including 4.5 sacks) through seven contests.

Update.Headline: Logs season-high 10 stops Week 8
Update.Notes: Murphy registered 10 tackles (eight solo) in a loss to the Lions on Sunday.
Update.Analysis: Murphy tied for third on Minnesota in tackles on a day when four Vikings finished with double-digit stops. The tackle tally was Murphy's highest of the season and snapped a four-game stretch of posting three stops or fewer. The veteran cornerback is enjoying a nice campaign overall, as he's tallied three interceptions so far, tying for second in the NFL in that category.

Update.Headline: Secures 13 stops in loss to Lions
Update.Notes: Metellus recorded 13 tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass in a Week 8 defeat against Detroit.
Update.Analysis: Metellus led Minnesota in tackles and recorded a season-high mark in the process. He's been a consistent presence for the Vikings' tough defense this season, playing every defensive snap in six of the team's seven contests so far. Metellus is up to 50 stops through seven games, putting him on pace for the third triple-digit tackle campaign of his career.

Update.Headline: Dominant despite defeat in Week 8
Update.Notes: Van Ginkel logged four tackles, including 2.5 sacks, in Sunday's loss to the Lions.
Update.Analysis: The Vikings lost their first game of the campaign, but their defense continued to be ferocious. That was largely due to Van Ginkel, who brought down Jared Goff three times -- two solo and one assisted -- in the first half. That pushed the veteran pass rusher up to 6.5 sacks on the season, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

Update.Headline: Tallies season-high 11 tackles Week 8
Update.Notes: Wilson registered 11 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's loss to Detroit.
Update.Analysis: Wilson finished second on the Vikings in stops, behind only Josh Metellus (13). One of his tackles was a sack of Jared Goff for a 10-yard loss on Detroit's first drive of the game, resulting in a Detroit punt. Wilson has 3.0 sacks through seven games, so he could surpass the career-best mark of 6.5 sacks he recorded over 17 regular-season games last year.

Update.Headline: Reportedly out for season with turf toe
Update.Notes: Huntley (toe) has reportedly sustained a season-ending turf toe injury, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
Update.Analysis: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter previously noted that Huntley could be a candidate for injured reserve, and Schefter's report suggests that such a transaction is looming. With star QB Lamar Jackson out indefinitely due to a right thumb injury, Joe Fagnano is in line make his first career NFL regular-season start Thursday night against the Jaguars, while Kedon Slovis is on hand to serve as his backup. Beyond that, it's likely that the Ravens will add further QB depth in the coming days.

Update.Headline: Set to resume practicing Wednesday
Update.Notes: The Patriots are expected to designate Hollins (calf) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
Update.Analysis: Hollins' last game appearance came back in Week 4, but with his return to practice on the horizon, he could be an option for the Patriots as soon as this Sunday's game against the Packers. With Romeo Doubs (shoulder) currently on IR and A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) availability for Week 9 looking cloudy, Hollins could have a chance at claiming a meaningful role right off the bat if he's cleared to play versus Green Bay. Prior to sustaining the calf injury, Hollins logged a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets through New England's first four games.

Update.Headline: Turns in reinstatement paperwork
Update.Notes: Aiyuk, who who currently is on the 49ers' Reserve/Left Squad list, has turned in paperwork to be reinstated, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
Update.Analysis: Per his agent Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk "is healthy and ready to get back on the field." Meanwhile, Schefter adds that once the wideout officially reports back to the 49ers, the team's options are to keep Aiyuk under his current contract, release him or look to move him ahead of this coming Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Given the moving parts involved, it remains to be seen when Aiyuk might return to the field in any locale, but depending on his health and conditioning level, the 2020 first-rounder could represent an intriguing option for a team looking to add WR depth to consider.

Update.Headline: Placed in concussion protocol
Update.Notes: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson has been placed in concussion protocol.
Update.Analysis: Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter of Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, and after being examined by an independent consultant he was cleared to return to the game. Though subsequent tests after the game and Monday morning showed no symptoms of a concussion, Watson informed the Browns on Tuesday morning that he was experiencing symptoms and was "immediately placed in the concussion protocol," per the team. Watson will need to clear the five-step protocol in order to play in Cleveland's Week 9 matchup with New Orleans, but if he's unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start at quarterback for the first time this season.

Update.Headline: Could start Week 9 with Watson in protocol
Update.Notes: Sanders could be needed to start Sunday's game at New Orleans after Deshaun Watson was placed in concussion protocol when he experienced symptoms Monday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
Update.Analysis: During this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson briefly departed the game in the first quarter after a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Jaquan Brisker. Sanders checked in and completed both of his pass attempts for two yards across four total plays before Watson was cleared to return for the Browns' next possession. However, with the concussion symptoms surfacing a day later, Watson's availability for Week 9 is now in jeopardy. Watson will still have time to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Sunday, but expect Sanders to at least get some reps in with the first-team offense Wednesday during the team's first practice of the week.

Update.Headline: Opens week with limited practice
Update.Notes: The Falcons listed Robinson (hamstring) as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
Update.Analysis: After landing in Spain early Wednesday in advance of Sunday's game versus the Bengals in Madrid, the Falcons opted to hold a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice. Robinson was able to do enough to garner a limited listing on the injury report, marking the first time since Week 7 that he's gone down as anything other than a non-participant in practice. If Robinson can get back to full activity Thursday or Friday, he'll put himself on track to be available as the top complement to lead back Bijan Robinson on Sunday.

Update.Headline: Trending toward game-time call Thursday
Update.Notes: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday that Tuten (ankle/foot) is feeling better, but the running back's status for Thursday's contest versus the Ravens is expected to come down to a game-time decision, John Shipley of SI.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Tuten was listed as a non-participant on the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, but he may be in line to take some reps during Wednesday's session. The 23-year-old looks poised to take a questionable tag into the team's matchup with Baltimore, but if he fares well in practice Wednesday and while working out early Thursday, he could get the green light to play on a short week. If Tuten suits up, it's conceivable that he handles a lighter workload than normal, after receiving no fewer than 15 touches in any of the Jaguars' first seven contests.

Update.Headline: Out for season after MCL surgery
Update.Notes: Kinlaw underwent season-ending surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Washington placed Kinlaw on injured reserve Tuesday, but it wasn't immediately known how much time the knee injury he initially sustained Week 6 would keep him out of commission. Now that Kinlaw has opted for surgery, he'll remain on IR for the Commanders' final 10 games in what amounts to another major hit to the defensive line. Washington also placed nose tackle Daron Payne on IR on Tuesday after he needed surgery to repair a Jones fracture in his left foot.

Update.Headline: Returning to practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Tyson (hamstring) is slated to resume practicing with the Saints on Wednesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
Update.Analysis: The Saints are expected to officially open the wide receiver's 21-day evaluation window as they kick off Week 9 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns. Given that the strained right hamstring has kept him off the field since Aug. 13, Tyson may need more than one week of practices to get himself back into playing shape, but the Saints haven't necessarily ruled the rookie first-round pick out from making his NFL debut against Cleveland. Whenever he's deemed ready to play, Tyson could immediately push Devaughn Vele for the Saints' No. 2 receiver job.

Update.Headline: Trending toward sitting out Week 9
Update.Notes: Watson is expected to face an uphill battle to clear concussion protocol prior to Sunday's game against the Saints, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the Browns' likely Week 9 starting quarterback, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
Update.Analysis: After reporting concussion symptoms Tuesday following Sunday's loss to the Steelers, Watson entered the protocol and isn't expected to practice Wednesday. Sanders will take all of the first-team reps Wednesday, and unless Watson can pass through the protocol quickly, the Browns will prepare for the second-year signal-caller to direct the offense in Week 9.

Update.Headline: Done for season with foot injury
Update.Notes: McNichols, who suffered a foot injury Sunday against the Eagles that may require surgery, is out for the season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
Update.Analysis: McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.

Update.Headline: Works on the side Wednesday
Update.Notes: Egbuka (foot) was spotted running on the side with a trainer Wednesday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
Update.Analysis: Egbuka, who last suited up for game action in Week 6, was limited at practice last Wednesday and Thursday before logging a DNP on Friday. It remains to be seen what his participation level will be as the week unfolds, but if Egbuka remains sidelined Sunday night against the Bears, Chris Godwin, Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson would be in line to lead Tampa Bay's Week 9 WR corps.

Update.Headline: Enters concussion protocol, day-to-day
Update.Notes: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Wilson is in the NFL's concussion protocol and is considered day-to-day, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Per Eric Allen of the Jets' official site, Wilson experienced symptoms of a concussion when he was evaluated Monday after taking a hard hit near the end of Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Jets. As a result, Wilson won't practice Wednesday, and his status for Sunday's road game against the Chiefs will need to be tracked closely in the coming days. If Wilson ends up being sidelined this weekend, added targets could be available for wideouts Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams and tight ends Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq.

Update.Headline: Set for limited practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Hall (quadriceps) will be a limited practice participant Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Hall, who hasn't played since Sept. 27, was also limited at practice last week, but Glenn said that the running back is "trending in the right direction" as Sunday's game against the Chiefs approaches, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com. As for how the workload might be split between Hall and Braelon Allen should Hall return this weekend, Glenn declined to go in specifics beyond noting that "both will play" in such a scenario, according to Cimini.

Update.Headline: No timetable for return
Update.Notes: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
Update.Analysis: Steichen said that Pierce, who has been on IR since Sept. 26, is currently rehabbing his injury, but the wideout's return is clearly not imminent. At 2-6, the Colts, who are already sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline, have little incentive to rush Pierce back. Meanwhile, fellow WR Josh Downs has asked to be dealt, a situation that further clouds the team's pass-catching corps ahead of Week 9.

Update.Headline: Making return to practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Parsons (knee) will be designated for return from the reserve/PUP list and will take part in individual work during Wednesday's practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Parsons will take part in practice for the first time in nearly 11 months, after a lengthy recovery from surgery to repair the ACL in his left knee, which he tore in a Dec. 14, 2025 game against the Broncos. Though LaFleur confirmed that Parsons has been cleared for full activity, the Packers are expected to limit the star edge rusher to individual work throughout Week 9. Parsons is then expected to advance to team work in Week 10, and if his knee continues to respond well to practice coming out of a Week 11 bye, he'll likely be activated from the PUP list to make his 2026 debut Nov. 25 versus the Rams.

Update.Headline: Set to kick Sunday
Update.Notes: Head coach Andy Reid said that Butker will remain the Chiefs' kicker for Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Butker -- who has made 12 of his 18 field-goal attempts in seven games this season -- converted one of his two tries along with with all three point-after attempts in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. Despite his recent accuracy issues, Butker will retain his kicking role this weekend, even though the Chiefs recently signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad.

Update.Headline: Set to miss Wednesday's practice
Update.Notes: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that Brown (knee/ankle) won't practice Wednesday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
Update.Analysis: Brown was sidelined for New England's Week 8 win over Miami, and with another absence from practice on tap, the wideout's status for Sunday's game against the Packers is cloudy. On the plus side for the Patriots, Mack Hollins (calf) could return from injured reserve this weekend to bolster a wideout corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams.

Update.Headline: Sitting out practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that Henderson (illness) won't practice Wednesday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
Update.Analysis: Henderson also didn't practice this past Thursday and Friday, and then missed the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins. The running back's absence to begin Week 9 prep suggests that he's no lock to play Sunday against the Packers, but Henderson's outlook on that front would no doubt improve with a return to the field within the next couple of days. While Henderson was sidelined in Miami, Rhamondre Stevenson paced New England's rushing attack, and Corey Kiner and Lan Larison mixed in behind him.

Update.Headline: Doesn't practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Head coach Todd Bowles said Egbuka (foot) didn't practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver was able to run on a side field, and the Buccaneers will see how he feels Thursday, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
Update.Analysis: Egbuka was able to clear ths concussion protocol last Friday, but he still missed this past Sunday's win against the Falcons due to a foot injury, marking a second absence in a row. Seemingly, Wednesday's bit of running is a test to get a sense of where Egbuka stands, health-wise, so Thursday's session could be revealing for his chances to return to action Sunday at Chicago.

Update.Headline: Not practicing Wednesday
Update.Notes: Skattebo (hamstring) didn't take part in Wednesday's practice and instead was seen working with a trainer on the side, Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports.
Update.Analysis: Skattebo tweaked his hamstring on his final carry during a Week 7 win at Houston, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he's kicking off Week 9 prep with a DNP. Head coach John Harbaugh told Raanan on Monday that Skattebo may be a game-time decision for Sunday's contest at Philadelphia, but he likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to put himself at least in that position. At the moment, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers are the Giants' healthy backfield options.

Update.Headline: Working with trainers Wednesday
Update.Notes: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Ferguson (ankle) will work with the Cowboys' training staff during Wednesday's practice, Briana Aldridge of CBS News Texas reports.
Update.Analysis: Such comments are an indication that Ferguson will go down as a DNP to kick off Week 9 prep, something that'll be revealed on Wednesday's injury report. Ferguson is tending to a low-ankle sprain in the wake of this past Sunday's loss to the Cardinals.

Update.Headline: Won't play in Week 9
Update.Notes: Head coach Mike Macdonald announced that Darnold won't play Sunday against the Cardinals due to a quadriceps injury, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports.
Update.Analysis: In addition to a quad issue that Darnold sustained late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Macdonald revealed that the quarterback suffered a rib injury early in that contest. The pair of health concerns may have played a part in Darnold's subpar performance, which included 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception on 17-for-34 passing and two carries for 20 yards. With Darnold out for the first time since Week 2, backup QB Drew Lock will draw the Week 9 start under center for the Seahawks.

Update.Headline: Set to start Sunday
Update.Notes: Lock (elbow) is slated to start Sunday's game against the Cardinals, per NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
Update.Analysis: Siciliano adds that Lock has an elbow injury that the team will manage during the week, but he's nonetheless set to get the starting assignment Sunday with fellow signal caller Sam Darnold unavailable due to quad and rib issues. Beyond this weekend, it's possible that Lock's QB1 stint could continue given that Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports that Darnold is viewed as week-to-week, according to coach Mike Macdonald.

Update.Headline: Not seen at practice
Update.Notes: Montgomery (groin) wasn't present for the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
Update.Analysis: Montgomery missed the Texans' two games before a Week 8 bye due to a groin issue, and his status remains up in the air as the team prepares for Sunday's contest at the Chargers. He hasn't practiced since sustaining the injury Oct. 11 at Tennessee, meaning he likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to suit up this weekend.

Update.Headline: Undergoes surgery
Update.Notes: Payne (foot) underwent season-ending surgery Wednesday, Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports.
Update.Analysis: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Payne will be out long-term with a foot injury suffered in practice. With both Javon Kinlaw (knee) and Payne out, Tim Settle will have a larger role at nose tackle going forward.

Update.Headline: Set to start Sunday
Update.Notes: Milton is set to be the Eagles' starting quarterback Sunday against the Giants, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
Update.Analysis: Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad Oct. 16, and less than a month later, he's getting the call after the Tanner McKee experience so far has resulted in three consecutive losses. In five appearances (no starts) between New England and Dallas in his career, Milton has competed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing 15 times for 66 yards and one TD and losing both of his fumbles.

Update.Headline: Playing time on upswing
Update.Notes: Sharp went without a target while playing 19 of the Buccaneers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.
Update.Analysis: After logging single-digit snaps on offense in each of the first six games of the season, Sharp appears to have firmly supplanted Ko Kieft as the Buccaneers' No. 3 tight end behind Cade Otton and Payne Durham. Sharp played a quarter of the snaps in a Week 7 win over the Buccaneers before bumping up to a season-high 32 percent share during Sunday's victory. The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU will likely continue to be utilized mainly as a blocker; he's drawn just one target (a 21-yard reception) while running only nine total routes so far this season.

Update.Headline: Benched for Joe Milton in Week 9
Update.Notes: McKee will shift to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Giants with the Eagles set to move forward with Joe Milton as their starting quarterback in Week 9, Adam Schefter of ESPN and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network report.
Update.Analysis: Just two days after announcing that McKee would draw a fourth straight start this weekend, head coach Nick Sirianni appears to have changed his tune. The Eagles' decision to move forward with Milton comes after McKee went 0-3 as a starter while completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 5.6 yards per attempt and a 2:2 TD:INT since replacing Jalen Hurts (calf) atop the depth chart. Since McKee is set to become a free agent next spring and may not be part of the Eagles' long-term plans, he could end up serving as the No. 3 quarterback if the team wants to give rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton the opportunity to suit up on game days.

Update.Headline: Signs to active roster
Update.Notes: The Browns signed Ryan to the active roster Wednesday from the team's practice squad.
Update.Analysis: Ryan has suited up seven times for the Browns so far this season. With another elevation ahead of Week 9, the 23-year-old is eligible to play for Cleveland once again against the Saints. He has spent the majority of his in-game snaps on special teams.

Update.Headline: Signs to practice squad
Update.Notes: The Browns signed Haskins to their practice squad Wednesday.
Update.Analysis: Haskins spent the majority of the 2026 season on New England's practice squad before being cut on Oct. 17. Last season with the Chargers, the 26-year-old recorded 17 rushing attempts for 47 yards, averaging 2.8 yards per carry. He also had four receptions for 13 yards.

Update.Headline: Sitting out first practice of Week 9
Update.Notes: Henry (foot) wasn't on the field for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Henry was unable to return to Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins after exiting in the second quarter due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided many details regarding the severity of the injury, but Henry will be sidelined as the team begins Week 9 prep. Henry will have two more chances to potentially practice this week before the Patriots decide whether he'll take a designation into Sunday's game against the Packers.

Update.Headline: Estimated as full participant
Update.Notes: Bowman was estimated as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
Update.Analysis: Bowman hasn't played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 6 against Chicago. Now with a full practice, the 23-year-old is on track to play Sunday against the Bengals. The second-year pro has six tackles (five solo) and two pass deflections in four games this season.

Update.Headline: Shipped to Baltimore
Update.Notes: The Ravens are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals that will send Brissett to Baltimore, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The deal is expected to be completed over the weekend.
Update.Analysis: Brissett was set to become a free agent this offseason and was demoted from the starting role earlier this week, making him an expendable piece for the Cardinals, who will move forward with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck as their quarterbacks. Baltimore, meanwhile, had a critical need for an experienced signal-caller after losing Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (foot) to injuries that will send both quarterbacks to injured reserve and potentially keep them out for the rest of the season, so Brissett will fill a void. Since the trade won't be made official for a few more days, Brissett won't be available for the Ravens' Thursday night game against the Jaguars. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will direct the Baltimore offense against Jacksonville, but Brissett could step in as the Ravens' new starter beginning with a Week 10 matchup against the Chargers.

Update.Headline: Signs to practice squad
Update.Notes: The Texans signed Sobkowicz to the practice squad Wednesday.
Update.Analysis: Sobkowicz was on Houston's practice squad for the first five weeks of the season before being cut in October. The 24-year-old has yet to make a regular-season appearance for the Texans. Landing back on the team's practice squad, the undrafted rookie has a long way to go before making his NFL debut.

Update.Headline: Questionable for Thursday after no practice
Update.Notes: Tuten (ankle/foot) is listed questionable for Thursday's game against the Ravens.
Update.Analysis: For the third day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on the Jaguars' injury report, even though head coach Liam Coen suggested the running back would practice in a limited fashion Wednesday, per Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network. The coach added that the Jaguars will be viewing Tuten as a game-time decision for Thursday's tilt, with his availability perhaps hinging on how he fares during a gameday workout. If Tuten ends up missing his first game of the season or is active but available in only a limited capacity, Chris Rodriguez would be in store for a larger role out of the backfield.

Update.Headline: Released from PS
Update.Notes: The Texans released Mitchell-Paden from the practice squad Wednesday.
Update.Analysis: Mitchell-Paden failed to appear in a 2026 regular-season game after signing to the Texans' practice squad to begin the campaign. In two games with the Saints in 2025, the 27-year-old recorded one reception for 14 yards on 55 total snaps (33 offensive).

Update.Headline: Joins Jets practice squad
Update.Notes: The Jets signed Manjack to the practice squad Wednesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
Update.Analysis: The undrafted rookie receiver out of TCU had previously spent time with Denver in the offseason, appearing in all three preseason games while catching three of four targets for 40 yards. After failing to make the Broncos' roster heading into Week 1, Manjack had been a free agent before landing an opportunity with the Jets.

Update.Headline: Not spotted at practice
Update.Notes: Barkley wasn't present for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Barkley may still be tending to the hamstring and back issues that he impacted his practice reps last week, but Wednesday's injury report will reveal if he indeed was a non-participant and also the reason for his absence. Jaydon Blue is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell tallied 11 carries for 34 yards and four catches (on six targets) for three yards while splitting the backfield with Barkley this past Sunday at Washington.

Update.Headline: Cleared to resume practicing
Update.Notes: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Njoku (fibula) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
Update.Analysis: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Njoku can be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. The veteran tight end has been out of action since sustaining the fibula injury Week 2, but if he's able to turn in a full practice at some point over the next three days, he could have a chance at being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Once he's back in the fold, Njoku could push Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps at tight end.

Update.Headline: Good to go for TNF
Update.Notes: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) does not carry an injury designation going into Thursday's game at the Ravens.
Update.Analysis: Though Meyers was limited in practice, the Jaguars are not listing him on the injury report going into Thursday's game. The veteran has battled through bumps and bruises throughout the season but has yet to miss a game. He'll be good to go for Week 9 in Charm City.

Update.Headline: No Week 9 injury designation
Update.Notes: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Ravens.
Update.Analysis: Meanwhile, Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) has been deemed questionable for the contest after being listed as a DNP on each of the Jaguars' injury reports, Monday through Wednesday. Given that Tuten has been the team's lead back this season, his playing status (and potential workload, if he's active Thursday) will provide valuable context related to the Week 9 fantasy prospects of Rodriguez, who could assume a larger backfield role versus Baltimore if Tuten ends up out or limited.

Update.Headline: Not present Wednesday
Update.Notes: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Smith has missed four of the last five contests due to a lingering hamstring injury, and until he's able to mix into drills again, he may not be a candidate to be active on game days. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye after Sunday's matchup with the Giants, so the team could be focusing on getting him healthy for Week 11 and beyond. In any case, fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also wasn't seen Wednesday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.

Update.Headline: Limited in practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Bailey (groin) was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Bailey was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, which is a step up from last week's three DNPs. The 23-year-old missed Week 8 with a groin injury suffered in Week 7 against Miami. Should the rookie continue to progress well throughout the week, he could have a shot at returning for Week 9.

Update.Headline: Not seen at practice
Update.Notes: Wicks (ankle) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Wicks has missed the last two games with an ankle injury and is trending towards being a DNP to start Week 9. If he's unable to ramp up his activity in the coming days, another missed game would be very much on the table. The Eagles are readying Joe Milton at quarterback, and he could be without both Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring), who was also absent from Wednesday's viewing period.

Update.Headline: Not practicing Wednesday
Update.Notes: Williams (hamstring) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
Update.Analysis: Williams missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury, which likely occurred at some point during the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers. However, head coach Todd Monken said he is "optimistic" that the 30-year-old will be ready for Week 9. Williams will need to upgrade his practice status by Friday for a chance to play.

Update.Headline: Will not practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: McCaffrey (hamstring) will not participate in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of Bay Area News Group reports.
Update.Analysis: Three key vets are not taking part in the first practice out of the bye Wednesday as McCaffrey, Mike Evans (Achilles/ribs) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) are all sidelined for this session. McCaffrey has been dealing with a hamstring issue since the Week 7 game in Atlanta. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that McCaffrey is "not going today but hopefully a chance [Thursday]." The next few days of practice will be telling for McCaffrey's status going into Sunday's game against the Raiders.

Update.Headline: Out for third straight game
Update.Notes: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Montgomery (groin) has made some progress but is still viewed as week-to-week and will remain out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
Update.Analysis: Montgomery missed Houston's last two games before a Week 8 bye, and he doesn't look like he'll be ready to return to action any sooner than Nov. 15, when the Texans face the Browns on the road. With Montgomery set to miss another game, Woody Marks is poised to maintain a lead role out of the backfield. While Montgomery was sidelined the previous two contests, Marks averaged 81.0 scrimmage yards on 18.5 touches per game.

Update.Headline: Won't practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (Achilles/ribs) won't practice Wednesday, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports.
Update.Analysis: Evans sat out a Week 7 loss in Atlanta after aggravating a right Achilles injury in Week 6 against the Commanders, and while there's an expectation that he'll be back after a Week 8 bye, he'll kick off this week with a DNP. He thus will have two more chances to mix into drills ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Raiders.

Update.Headline: No practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Samuel (hamstring) won't take part in practice Wednesday, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
Update.Analysis: Samuel injured his right hamstring during a Week 5 win at Seattle, resulting in two missed games before the 49ers' Week 8 bye. Head coach Kyle Shanahan relayed to Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area on Oct. 26 that Samuel has a chance to return this Sunday against the Raiders, but Shanahan's tone was a bit different Wednesday, when he told Vic Tafur and Matt Barrows of The Athletic that Samuel doesn't seem as close to playing as fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles).

Update.Headline: Does not practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Franklin (shin) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Franklin started the week as a nonparticipant in practice Wednesday and hasn't played since Week 6 after suffering a hairline fracture in his shin. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur added Wednesday that the 30-year-old is making progress in his recovery and he hopes Franklin can return soon. The ninth-year pro has 41 tackles (18 solo), one pass deflection and one forced fumble in six games this season.

Update.Headline: Limited at Wednesday's walkthrough
Update.Notes: St. Brown was a limited participant at Wednesday's walkthrough due to a rib injury, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
Update.Analysis: St. Brown made a brief exit during this past Sunday's win against the Vikings due to an undisclosed injury but was able to return, finishing with seven catches (on eight targets) for 46 yards and one carry for 10 yards. The nature of the health concern has been revealed, but his ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday generally bodes well for his status ahead of Sunday's game at Miami.

Update.Headline: Sits out first Week 9 practice
Update.Notes: Wright (quadriceps) was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
Update.Analysis: In addition to a foot injury, Wright was listed with the same quad issue on the Dolphins' Week 8 injury report but proceeded to log three full practices before playing in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Though he played just 13 total snaps between offense and special teams in Week 8, Wright apparently emerged from the contest with his quad injury still bothering him. He'll have two more chances to get back to full practice participation prior to this Sunday's game against the Lions.

Update.Headline: Does not practice Wednesday
Update.Notes: Skattebo (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
