Update.Analysis: Nabers was spotted working with the Giants' training staff during the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, one day removed from not being on the team's initial Week 9 injury report. The reason for his likely practice restrictions isn't known but will be revealed once New York posts its second injury report of the week.

Update.Headline: Misses practice Thursday
Update.Notes: Nixon (groin) did not practice Thursday, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
Update.Analysis: After being limited Wednesday, Nixon downgraded to DNP and appears to be at risk of missing Sunday's game against the Patriots. It's a new injury for Nixon, so it's possible he was injured in practice this week. Benjamin St-Juste and Carrington Valentine would be in line for increased snaps if Nixon needs to sit.

Update.Headline: Another DNP on Thursday
Update.Notes: Monangai (thumb/toe) didn't practice Thursday.
Update.Analysis: Monangai also missed Wednesday's walkthrough due to the turf-toe injury that has sidelined him the last four contests. With no activity to speak of so far and just one more chance to practice this week, he seems to be trending toward another absence Sunday against the Buccaneers, something that may be confirmed on Friday's injury report. D'Andre Swift will continue to pace the Bears backfield for as long as Monangai is sidelined, with Roschon Johnson on hand for any RB reps that linger.

Update.Headline: DNP on Thursday
Update.Notes: Davis-Gaither (knee) did not practice Thursday, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
Update.Analysis: That's back-to-back DNPs to open the practice week for Davis-Gaither, who has started all eight games this season. He's piled up 65 tackles (33 solo) and one pass breakup on 92 percent of the Colts' defensive snaps.

Update.Headline: Upgrades to full practice
Update.Notes: Egbuka (foot) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
Update.Analysis: After missing Wednesday's practice, Egbuka was back in the mix in full on Thursday. The second-year wideout has missed the last two games due to a concussion and a foot injury, but appears to be on track to return Sunday in Chicago. Getting Egbuka back in the fold would be a boon for a Buccaneers' passing game which has yet to hit its stride this season.

Update.Headline: Full practice Thursday
Update.Notes: Gainwell (hip) was a full practice participant Thursday, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
Update.Analysis: Gainwell also tended to a hip injury last week, when he got back to full by Friday, but he still entered the weekend listed as questionable for Week 8 action. He proceeded to suit up this past Sunday against the Falcons and split Tampa Bay's backfield with Bucky Irving, logging a 50 percent snap share and going for 140 yards on 25 carries in rainy conditions. Considering Gainwell followed up Wednesday's limited session with an uncapped one Thursday, he's good to go for Sunday's road showdown with the Bears.

Update.Headline: Set to play Sunday amid trade rumors
Update.Notes: Taylor was a full participant at Thursday's practice, and Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports that both Taylor and head coach Shane Steichen have maintained that Taylor will play Sunday against the Cowboys despite ongoing trade rumors surrounding the star running back.
Update.Analysis: "You can't avoid it," Taylor said of the trade rumors. "But it's more about trying to block that out." Taylor's preparing for what could well be his last game as a member of the Colts. Per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, the 2-6 Colts have received trade calls on numerous players including Taylor, but Indianapolis doesn't intend to complete any additional trades prior to the conclusion of Sunday's game.

Update.Headline: Back at practice Thursday
Update.Notes: Carter (illness) returned to practice Thursday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
Update.Analysis: Carter was absent Wednesday, but his return to the practice field puts the edge rusher on track for Sunday's game against the Eagles. Carter has started all seven games this season, recording 18 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble on 88 percent of the defensive snaps.

Update.Headline: Returns to practice Thursday
Update.Notes: Kamara (rest/back) returned to practice Thursday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
Update.Analysis: The veteran was back on the field Thursday after getting a rest day to open the practice week. Kamara has also dealt with a back issue that limited his practice participation in recent weeks. The Saints are coming off a bye, so the added time off likely bodes well for Kamara being closer to full strength heading into Week 9 against the Browns. New Orleans' practice report will provide insight on Kamara's participation level, but he seems to be trending in the right direction regardless.

Update.Headline: Does not practice Thursday
Update.Notes: Wilson (concussion) did not practice Thursday.
Update.Analysis: Wilson remains in concussion protocol and has not practiced either day thus far this week. He was placed in protocol midweek, which makes it an uphill climb for him to be cleared for Sunday's game at the Chiefs. If Wilson can't clear protocol, fantasy managers can expect more targets for Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper.

Update.Headline: Practices fully Thursday
Update.Notes: Hall (quadriceps) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
Update.Analysis: After opening the week with a limited session, Hall upgraded to full participation Thursday, indicating that he's in the clear to return Sunday against the Chiefs for his first action since Week 3. Braelon Allen has thrived in the lead role during Hall's absence, and offensive coordinator Frank Reich said Thursday that the Jets intend to utilize "a mix" of the two running backs Sunday, per Al Iannazzone of Newsday Sports. Hall is the superior receiving back, but Allen is averaging 5.0 yards per carry while Hall averaged just 3.2 YPC prior to getting hurt.

Update.Headline: Back practicing in full
Update.Notes: Taylor (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
Update.Analysis: Taylor was limited Wednesday, but his return to full Thursday puts him on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. The tight end has been a surprisingly big part of the passing offense this season despite the selection of Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's Draft. Taylor has secured 17 of 23 targets for 136 yards and two touchdowns across six games.

Update.Headline: Officially elevated Thursday
Update.Notes: The Ravens elevated Moody from the practice squad for Thursday night's game against the Jaguars.
Update.Analysis: With Tyler Loop (groin) sent to injured reserve this week, Moody will handle kicking duties for Baltimore for the foreseeable future. With Joe Fagnano at the controls of the offense against Jacksonville, Moody is not an exciting fantasy bet.

Update.Headline: Suited up for Thursday's practice
Update.Notes: McCaffrey (hamstring) was present for the open portion of Thursday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
Update.Analysis: McCaffrey was hampered by a left hamstring injury during the 49ers' last game, a Week 7 loss in Atlanta. Even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he didn't practice Wednesday, after which he touched on the health concern. "I had no idea (it was a hamstring injury)," he told Vic Tafur and Matt Barrows of The Athletic. "It wasn't too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great." Thursday's practice report will reveal how much work McCaffrey was able to handle.

Update.Headline: Misses open portion Thursday
Update.Notes: Evans (Achilles) did not participate in the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Evans' absence Thursday comes as no surprise considering GM John Lynch stated earlier in the day that Evans is unlikely to return Sunday against the Raiders. Barring an unexpectedly quick recovery, Evans will sit out a second consecutive game sandwiched around San Francisco's Week 8 bye before possible returning in Week 10 at Dallas. At 6-1, the 49ers can afford to take a cautious approach with the top option in their injury-riddled wide receiver room.

Update.Headline: Not spotted Thursday
Update.Notes: Samuel (hamstring) did not participate in the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Samuel hasn't played or practiced since sustaining a hamstring injury in San Francisco's Week 5 win over the Seahawks. He'll likely require at least some ramp-up period upon returning to practice, and GM John Lynch indicated Thursday that Samuel is expected to sit out Sunday's game against the Raiders. Samuel's likely to be formally ruled out on Friday's injury report.

Update.Headline: Officially placed on IR
Update.Notes: The Ravens have officially placed Jackson (thumb)on injured reserve.
Update.Analysis: Prior to Thursday night's game against the Jaguars, the Ravens made a trio of moves to re-shape their Week 9 QB corps. Along with Jackson, Tyler Huntley (toe) landed on IR, while Austin Reed was added to the team's active roster. As a result, Joe Fagnano (Thursday's starter), Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed are available to face Jacksonville, and then in the coming days Jacoby Brissett will be on his way to Baltimore via a looming trade with the Cardinals.

Update.Headline: Remains limited Thursday
Update.Notes: St. Brown (ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
Update.Analysis: St. Brown maintained his activity level from Wednesday's walkthrough as he navigates a rib injury, which was likely the reason for his brief time on the sideline this past Sunday against the Vikings. He thus has one more chance to get back to full Friday, or else he'll be at risk of entering the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Miami.

Update.Headline: Sent to injured reserve
Update.Notes: The Bears placed Scott (wrist) on injured reserve Thursday.
Update.Analysis: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

Update.Headline: Joins Lamar on IR
Update.Notes: Huntley (toe) was placed on injured reserve Thursday.
Update.Analysis: Huntley and Lamar Jackson (thumb) were both placed on injured reserve Thursday. The latter still has at least a slim chance to return this season, while Huntley's injury has been confirmed to be season-ending. Joe Fagnano is set to start Thursday's game against the Jaguars before reinforcements arrive under center in the form of Jacoby Brissett, for whom the Ravens are expected to finalize a trade over the weekend.

Update.Headline: DNP due to knee injury
Update.Notes: Nabers didn't practice Thursday due to a knee injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
Update.Analysis: Nabers opened Thursday's session working on the side with trainers, and afterward he told Art Stapleton of USA Today, "I'll be good," as it pertains to his status for Week 9. In any case, the reason for Nabers' absence is a knee issue, which could be related to the right ACL tear that ended his 2025 season in Week 4. He'll have one more chance to prove his health Friday, at which point the Giants may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

Update.Headline: Added to Week 9 injury report
Update.Notes: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
Update.Analysis: Fannin wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so his appearance on it a day later is notable. It remains to be seen if Thursday's listed limitations were maintenance-related or indicative of a setback, but the tight end may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Saints without an injury designation.

Update.Headline: Remains limited Thursday
Update.Notes: Tyson (hamstring) remained a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Tyson has logged consecutive limited practices since having his 21-day window to return from IR opened Wednesday. The rookie first-round pick could make his NFL regular-season debut as soon as Sunday against the Browns, though the Saints would probably want him to log at least one full practice before seeing game action, so it's more likely that Tyson's debut will be delayed at least one more week. His return to action would be proceeded by an official move adding Tyson to the 53-man roster.

Update.Headline: Remains sidelined at practice
Update.Notes: Skattebo (hamstring) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
Update.Analysis: Coming out of New York's Week 8 bye, Skattebo hasn't been able to practice this week due to the hamstring injury that he suffered near the end of a Week 7 win at Houston. Friday's injury report will reveal his odds to suit up Sunday at Philadelphia, but if Skattebo is inhibited or sidelined, Devin Singletary is the next player up in the Giants backfield, Greg Desrosiers is the only other RB on the active roster, and Eric Gray and Phil Mafah are candidates to be elevated from the practice squad.

Update.Headline: Remains limited Thursday
Update.Notes: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
Update.Analysis: Boston dealt with a foot issue a couple weeks ago, but the calf injury is new this week. The rookie wideout has been scuffling after a hot start to the season. Perhaps the likely insertion of Shedeur Sanders this Sunday against the Saints can help Boston regain his big-play ability. Boston is a low-floor, upside WR4 for fantasy.

Update.Headline: Full participant Thursday
Update.Notes: Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced without limitations Thursday.
Update.Analysis: Rice is off the injury report Thursday after kicking off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday. The oft-injured wide receiver has been limited to five appearances this season, one of which he left before recording a catch, but he has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns across the other four games. With Rice getting healthier, he could feast Sunday against a Jets defense that's allowing 30.7 points per game during an active three-game losing streak.

Update.Headline: Stays limited Thursday
Update.Notes: Watson (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Watson now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt to begin Week 9 prep, which stems from the broken rib that he suffered during last Thursday's win against the Panthers. He'll have one more chance Friday to get back to full participation, at which point the Packers may tag him with a designation for Sunday's contest at New England.

Update.Headline: Thursday's DNP confirmed
Update.Notes: Brown (ankle/knee) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Thursday's injury report confirms Brown's absence after he wasn't spotted earlier in the day. Brown has missed the team's first two practices leading up to Sunday's game against the Packers, suggesting he's fighting an uphill battle in his effort to avoid missing a second consecutive game. He has dressed for only three of New England's first eight games. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and possibly Mack Hollins (calf) would lead the Patriots' wide receiver room Sunday if Brown sits again.

Update.Headline: Logs full practice Thursday
Update.Notes: Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
Update.Analysis: Kelce was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, but the tight end's full participation Thursday paves the way for him to be in uniform Sunday against the Jets. Over his last two games, the Chiefs' leader in catches and receiving yards has amassed nine catches on 15 targets for 111 yards with a TD, and as long as he stays healthy he'll merit weekly fantasy lineup consideration.

Update.Headline: Limited Thursday
Update.Notes: Kamara (rest/back) was limited at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Kamara followed up Wednesday's absence from practice with some activity one day later as he eases into the week due to a lingering back issue. Friday's injury report will reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Update.Headline: Dealing with knee issue
Update.Notes: Lloyd was limited at practice Thursday due to a knee injury.
Update.Analysis: Lloyd's addition to the Packers' practice report midweek is something to monitor, especially because it may indicate a health concern that occurred during Thursday's session. Ultimately, Friday's injury report may provide some clarity into the situation.

Update.Headline: Limited Wednesday
Update.Notes: Ogletree (knee) upgraded to a limited practice Thursday.
Update.Analysis: After being a DNP on Wednesday, Ogletree's return to practice puts him on track for Sunday's game against Dallas. The Colts are using four tight ends most weeks, featuring Tyler Warren in the passing game, while Mo Alie-Cox, Ogletree and Will Mallory play part-time roles.

Update.Headline: Logs another 'DNP' Thursday
Update.Notes: Henderson (illness) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, ESPN's Rob Demovsky reports.
Update.Analysis: Henderson officially goes down as a non-participant for a second consecutive Week 9 practice and has now missed a full week due to this illness. His participation level will be worth monitoring Friday, though it looks likely at this point that Henderson will carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Packers. Corey Kiner would be in line to maintain an expanded role alongside Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson sits again Sunday.

Update.Headline: Downgraded to DNP on Thursday
Update.Notes: Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) did not practice Thursday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: After being limited Wednesday, Donaldson's downgrade to DNP puts him in jeopardy of missing Week 9 against the Browns. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) also looking unlikely to play, the Saints could be rolling with Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and Audric Estime out of the backfield.

Update.Headline: Expected to play Thursday
Update.Notes: Tuten (ankle/foot) 'should be' available for Thursday night's game against the Ravens barring any pregame setbacks, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
Update.Analysis: Tuten logged 'DNP' listings on all three of the Jaguars' Week 9 injury reports ahead of the contest and had been considered a game-time decision. Fowler's report indicates that the running back is trending toward active status, but those considering Tuten in Week 9 fantasy lineups will nonetheless want to verify his playing status ahead of Thursday's 8:15 pm ET kickoff.

Update.Headline: Another limited session
Update.Notes: Pickens (hamstring) was limited at Thursday's practice, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Pickens maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he deals with lingering shoulder and hamstring injuries. He still was able to handle a 57 percent snap share this past Sunday against the Cardinals, but he mustered only two catches (on four targets) for 48 yards. Friday's practice report will unveil whether or not Pickens heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Indianapolis.

Update.Headline: Remains unavailable Thursday
Update.Notes: Ferguson (ankle) did not practice Thursday, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Ferguson's back-to-back absences to kick off Week 9 prep don't bode well for his availability Sunday against the Colts. He sustained a low-ankle sprain after playing just four snaps during Dallas' Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Brevyn Spann-Ford worked as the team's top TE after Ferguson's exit. Ferguson will have one more opportunity to practice Friday before Dallas posts Week 9 game statuses.

Update.Headline: Upgrades to full practice
Update.Notes: Bailey (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
Update.Analysis: After missing Week 8 with the groin injury he suffered the previous week, Bailey appears poised to return after missing just one contest. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Bailey has piled up 35 tackles (21 solo), including 5.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.

Update.Headline: Limited Thursday
Update.Notes: Wright (quadriceps) was limited in Thursday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
Update.Analysis: Wright has been battling various issues all season and hasn't been effective when on the field, yet he's still operating as the Dolphins' lightly-used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon. Wright is averaging a microscopic 1.9 yards per carry this season.

Update.Headline: Limited participant Thursday
Update.Notes: Moore (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
Update.Analysis: Moore mustered some level of activity in Buffalo's first practice of Week 9 after downplaying the knee injury that forced him out late in the Week 8 win over Baltimore. He has an extra day to recover before the Bills face the Vikings on MNF. Moore has two more chances to practice without limitations and put himself in the clear to suit up.

Update.Headline: Limited at practice Thursday
Update.Notes: Kincaid (chest) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice,.
Update.Analysis: Fellow pass catchers DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (shoulder) were also limited Thursday, so the trio's status will need to be monitored ahead of Monday night's game against the Vikings. Over his last two outings, Kincaid has managed to make his mark from a fantasy perspective by logging an 11/124/1 receiving line in that span.

Update.Headline: DNP on Thursday
Update.Notes: Palmer (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
Update.Analysis: The veteran wideout was injured in Sunday's win over the Ravens and was unable to return to the contest. If he's unable to play Monday night against the Vikings, Skyler Bell and Greg Dortch could see additional work on offense.

Update.Headline: Limited Thursday
Update.Notes: Coleman (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.
Update.Analysis: It's a new injury for Coleman, who is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4. With both DJ Moore (knee) and Dalton Kincaid (chest) healthy last Sunday against the Ravens, Coleman caught just one pass for four yards on three targets.

Update.Headline: Signed to 53-man roster
Update.Notes: Reed was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster ahead of Thursday's game against Jacksonville.
Update.Analysis: With Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve and Jacoby Brissett unavailable after recently being acquired from the Cardinals, the Ravens added Reed to bolster depth at the quarterback position. Reed will be behind Joe Fagnano and Kedon Slovis, and while that doesn't mean he will be active, he should at least be available if needed as Baltimore's emergency signal-caller.

Update.Headline: Sick Thursday
Update.Notes: Johnson (illness) did not practice Thursday.
Update.Analysis: Johnson will have an extra day to rest up this week, as the Bills host the Vikings on Monday night. Buffalo's preferred pass-catching back, Johnson has rushed six times for just 10 yards through six games this season, but has caught all 15 of his targets for 174 yards.
